_comment: Advisory Features module. Rule-based, auditable, tunable without code changes - same contract as severity_config.json and recommendation_config.json. Advisory Features answers 'what should I generally know or watch for over time'; Preventive Care answers 'what do I do about this elevated risk score now'. Every phrase here is emitted only when its named upstream data point is present.

lifestyle_advisory._comment: Keyed on chronic-risk model feature codes. Emitted only when the feature appears among a flagged condition's top drivers AND the patient's value crosses trigger_value. 'direction' says which side of the value triggers it. min_importance is deliberately low: it filters noise, not modest-importance factors that happen to be highly modifiable (smoking scores ~0.008 here).

_BMI5.label: Body weight
_BMI5.advisory: Body mass index sits above the healthy range and is one of the strongest contributors to your screening risk. Sustained loss of 5-10% of body weight measurably lowers risk across diabetes, cardiovascular and joint outcomes.
_BMI5.standing_guidance: Aim for gradual change - 0.5 kg per week is sustainable; faster loss is usually regained.

_SMOKER3.label: Smoking
_SMOKER3.advisory: Current smoking is among the top contributors to your screening risk. It is also the single factor with the fastest measurable benefit from change - cardiovascular risk begins falling within weeks of stopping.
_SMOKER3.standing_guidance: Combined behavioural support and pharmacotherapy roughly doubles quit success compared with willpower alone.

EXERANY2.label: Physical activity
EXERANY2.advisory: No physical activity was recorded in the last 30 days, and inactivity is contributing to your screening risk.
EXERANY2.standing_guidance: 150 minutes per week of moderate activity is the usual target, but the largest risk reduction comes from moving from none to some - not from reaching the target.

_TOTINDA.label: Physical activity
_TOTINDA.advisory: Recorded activity is below the level associated with lower chronic risk in this cohort.
_TOTINDA.standing_guidance: Short, frequent activity counts; it does not need to be continuous or vigorous.

GENHLTH.label: Self-rated health
GENHLTH.advisory: Self-rated general health of 'Fair' or 'Poor' is one of the strongest single predictors in this model - it independently tracks outcomes even after other factors are accounted for.
GENHLTH.standing_guidance: Worth raising directly with a clinician, since it often reflects something not yet captured in a specific diagnosis.

BPHIGH4.label: Blood pressure
BPHIGH4.advisory: A previous high blood pressure reading is contributing to your screening risk. Hypertension is asymptomatic until it causes damage, so it is managed by measurement rather than by how you feel.
BPHIGH4.standing_guidance: Home monitoring at a consistent time of day gives a more useful trend than occasional clinic readings.

TOLDHI2.label: Cholesterol
TOLDHI2.advisory: A previous high cholesterol result is contributing to your screening risk, and lipid levels are also asymptomatic.
TOLDHI2.standing_guidance: Reducing saturated fat and increasing soluble fibre both act on LDL; effect sizes are modest individually and additive together.

DRNK3GE5.label: Alcohol
DRNK3GE5.advisory: Reported heavy drinking episodes are contributing to your screening risk, with effects on liver, blood pressure and cardiac rhythm.
DRNK3GE5.standing_guidance: Drink-free days reduce cumulative exposure more reliably than reducing the amount per occasion.

MENTHLTH.label: Mental wellbeing
MENTHLTH.advisory: Several mentally unwell days were reported in the last month, and this is contributing to your screening risk.
MENTHLTH.standing_guidance: Mental and physical risk factors compound each other; addressing either tends to help the other.

ALCDAY5.label: Alcohol
ALCDAY5.advisory: Drinking on this many days per month is contributing to your screening risk, with effects on liver, blood pressure and cardiac rhythm.
ALCDAY5.standing_guidance: Drink-free days reduce cumulative exposure more reliably than cutting the amount per occasion.

PHYSHLTH.label: Physical wellbeing
PHYSHLTH.advisory: Several physically unwell days were reported in the last month, and this is contributing to your screening risk.
PHYSHLTH.standing_guidance: A pattern of unwell days is worth reviewing as a whole rather than episode by episode.

screening_reminders._comment: Age- and risk-profile-based STANDING screening guidance, independent of the current symptom assessment. 'requires_risk_factor' means the reminder only appears when one of the named chronic conditions is flagged by the risk model. All are phrased as 'discuss with a clinician' - intervals vary by country and guideline body, so no specific interval is asserted.

reminders.advisory: Blood pressure should be checked periodically in all adults, and more often where other cardiovascular risk factors are present.
Adults over 40 with elevated cardiovascular risk factors should discuss formal cardiovascular risk assessment - including lipids and blood pressure - with a doctor.
Adults over 35 with elevated metabolic risk factors should discuss blood glucose or HbA1c screening with a doctor.
Colorectal cancer screening is generally offered from age 45. If you have not been invited, it is worth asking.
Cervical screening is offered to women in this age range. Attendance is worth confirming even when you feel well.
Breast screening is generally offered from age 40-50 depending on local guidance. Worth asking which applies to you.
Where diabetes or hypertension is present, periodic kidney function and urine protein testing is recommended - kidney disease is silent early on.
Any new, changing or non-healing skin lesion warrants review regardless of age or screening schedule.
Periodic mental health review is worth raising with a clinician, particularly where physical symptoms are recurrent.
Bone density assessment is generally considered from age 65, or earlier where fracture risk factors are present.

symptom_trend._comment: Cross-session pattern detection. A single assessment cannot see these, which is why they belong here rather than in Preventive Care. min_sessions is the minimum history required before ANY trend claim is made - below it the sub-section is omitted rather than shown empty.
symptom_trend.escalation_advisory: '{symptom}' has now been reported in {count} of your last {total} assessments. A recurring symptom is a different clinical question from a one-off one, and is worth raising as a pattern rather than as separate episodes.
symptom_trend.recurring_disease_advisory: {disease} has been the leading prediction in {count} of your last {total} assessments. Repeated prediction is not confirmation, but it is worth bringing the pattern to a clinician.
symptom_trend.severity_trend_advisory: Triage severity has been rising across your recent assessments ({trend}). Worth review even if each individual assessment seemed manageable.

condition_education._comment: Educational reframing of disease_lookup fields ALREADY in the system. Deliberately not prescriptive: 'cures' is presented as what care typically involves, never as an instruction to the patient. Emitted only where the lookup actually holds the field. typical_profile_template is the fallback when no disease_lookup entry exists: it is sourced from the disease model's own symptom-evidence profile, which covers all predicted conditions.
condition_education.typical_care_template: Care for this condition typically involves {cures}. This is general information about how the condition is usually approached, not a treatment instruction for you.
condition_education.specialist_template: This condition is usually managed by: {doctor}.
condition_education.risk_template: Recorded risk level for this condition in our reference data: {risk_level}.
condition_education.closing_note: Educational information only. It describes the condition in general terms and is not advice about your individual case.
condition_education.typical_profile_template: This condition is characterised in our reference data by: {symptoms}. Your reported symptoms matched {matched} of these.

behavioral_nudges._comment: Standing nudges tied to the SPECIFIC top risk-driving factors computed by the chronic risk model. Only emitted for factors that actually appear as drivers - never as a generic checklist.

_SMOKER3.title: Smoking cessation
_SMOKER3.nudge: Ask a clinician or pharmacist about NHS/local quit services, nicotine replacement and prescription options. Support plus medication outperforms either alone.

_BMI5.title: Weight management
_BMI5.nudge: A referral to a structured weight-management or dietetic programme is available in most systems and outperforms unsupported dieting.

EXERANY2.title: Getting started with activity
EXERANY2.nudge: Begin with walking most days and build gradually. Ask about supervised exercise programmes if a cardiac or joint condition makes you cautious about starting.

_TOTINDA.title: Building activity
_TOTINDA.nudge: Increasing activity from none to any level gives the largest single risk reduction. Ask about local activity referral schemes.

DRNK3GE5.title: Alcohol reduction
DRNK3GE5.nudge: Ask a clinician about brief intervention support. Tracking units for two weeks is usually more informative than estimating from memory.

GENHLTH.title: Whole-health review
GENHLTH.nudge: Book a general review rather than a single-symptom appointment - low self-rated health often reflects several small things at once.

MENTHLTH.title: Mental health support
MENTHLTH.nudge: Ask about talking-therapy self-referral, which does not require a GP appointment in many systems.

BPHIGH4.title: Blood pressure monitoring
BPHIGH4.nudge: A validated home monitor and a week of morning readings gives a clinician far more to work with than a single clinic measurement.

ALCDAY5.title: Alcohol reduction
ALCDAY5.nudge: Ask a clinician about brief intervention support. Tracking units for two weeks is usually more informative than estimating from memory.

PHYSHLTH.title: Recurrent unwell days
PHYSHLTH.nudge: Bring the pattern of unwell days to a review rather than each episode separately - the trend is the useful information.

TOLDHI2.title: Cholesterol review
TOLDHI2.nudge: Ask when your lipids were last measured and what the target is for your risk level; both change with overall cardiovascular risk.

disclaimer: Advisory information is general health guidance derived from your risk profile and assessment history. It is not personalised medical advice, not a diagnosis, and does not replace review by a qualified clinician.
